title: kubestream — Object Timeline
description: The life of one Kubernetes object as kubestream recorded it: every row it wrote, the diff each row carried, who the field managers were, and what Kubernetes itself was saying about the object at the same moments. This is the post-mortem view — pick the object, set the time range to the incident, and read down. Reads the ClickHouse the operator writes to; see docs/QUERIES.md for the same questions as copy-paste SQL.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The ClickHouse holding kubestream's resource_states table.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: cluster_id is the leading column of the sort key, so every panel filters on it. Selecting one is not optional: without it a query both scans the whole table and silently mixes clusters.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

list.name: kind
list.label: Kind
list.description: Kind alone, not group/kind: kubestream's identity key is version-agnostic and a kind name is unique in practice within a cluster. If you do run two same-named kinds from different API groups, add an api_group filter to the panels.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Empty string for cluster-scoped objects — it is a real value in this column, not a null, so it appears in the list as a blank option.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} AND kind = ${kind:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} AND kind = ${kind:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

list.name: name
list.label: Name
list.description: The object. Names are reused across delete-and-recreate cycles, so a single name can cover several incarnations; the Latest recorded state panel shows which uid is current, and the rows table shows where one incarnation ends and the next begins.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} AND kind = ${kind:sqlstring} AND namespace = ${namespace:sqlstring} ORDER BY name

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} AND kind = ${kind:sqlstring} AND namespace = ${namespace:sqlstring} ORDER BY name

panels.title: Changes over time
panels.description: One series per event_type, bucketed to the dashboard's interval. This is the shape of the object's life: a flat line of nothing, then a cluster of Modified rows around a deploy, then whatever happened next. Checkpoint counts as a change because it is one — a Checkpoint is a Modified that also carries full state.

panels.title: Field managers
panels.description: Who touched this object in the window, by number of rows their manager name appears on. actors is harvested from metadata.managedFields, so it is 'who probably changed this' rather than an audit-grade attribution — several managers own different parts of the same object and all of them are credited on every row. Deleted rows carry no actors by design and so never appear here.

panels.title: Latest recorded state
panels.description: The object's newest row by event time, read as an argMax aggregate over its whole history so the result does not depend on the order rows were inserted in. sha256 is the digest of the operator's normalized JSON and is what a reconstruction should be checked against; incarnations above 1 means this name has been deleted and recreated, and everything here describes the newest incarnation only.

panels.title: Rows and diffs
panels.description: Every row kubestream wrote for this object, newest first, with the change each one carried. Modified rows carry an RFC 6902 patch in diff; Added, Snapshot and Checkpoint rows carry full state in data instead, and are shown as a byte count because the whole object is too large to read in a table cell — click through to the query in docs/QUERIES.md to read one. Deleted rows carry neither.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    ts,
    event_type,
    uid,
    resource_version,
    arrayStringConcat(arraySort(actors), ', ') AS field_managers,
    multiIf(
        diff != '', diff,
        data != '', concat('(full state, ', toString(length(data)), ' bytes)'),
        ''
    ) AS change,
    sha256
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND kind = ${kind:sqlstring}
  AND namespace = ${namespace:sqlstring}
  AND name = ${name:sqlstring}
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 500

panels.title: Kubernetes Events for this object
panels.description: What the cluster was saying about the object over the same window, for the case where the change rows alone do not explain the incident. Requires a rule streaming v1/Event or events.k8s.io/v1/Event; the panel is empty otherwise. Matched on the Event's subject name and kind rather than its uid, so Events for an earlier incarnation of this name still show up — that is usually what you want in a post-mortem.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    ts,
    JSONExtractString(data, 'type')    AS severity,
    JSONExtractString(data, 'reason')  AS reason,
    JSONExtractString(data, 'message') AS message,
    greatest(
        JSONExtractUInt(data, 'count'),
        JSONExtractUInt(data, 'deprecatedCount'),
        JSONExtractUInt(data, 'series', 'count')
    ) AS occurrences
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND kind = 'Event'
  AND namespace = ${namespace:sqlstring}
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND coalesce(
        nullIf(JSONExtractString(data, 'involvedObject', 'name'), ''),
        nullIf(JSONExtractString(data, 'regarding',      'name'), '')
      ) = ${name:sqlstring}
  AND coalesce(
        nullIf(JSONExtractString(data, 'involvedObject', 'kind'), ''),
        nullIf(JSONExtractString(data, 'regarding',      'kind'), '')
      ) = ${kind:sqlstring}
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 200
